entry:fsf:cov:eval.note: v3.1 is still current (gdm-fs#g1, #g2). Pre-deployment assessment (fsf31#f1) and alert/periodic assessments, methodology in the framework, and involvement of external parties (fsf31#f4) are supported. The missing piece from Oct is now found: Google DeepMind states it has partnered with UK AISI since Nov 2023 'to test our most capable models' (gdm-aisi#a1, #a2); the Gemini 3.7 Flash report describes independent external testing (flash37#r2). The note does not claim AISI testing is pre-deployment.

entry:fsf:cov:acct.note: Factual core supported by v3.1 (still current): internal legal, compliance and safety reviews with escalation (fsf31#f2); aim to share information with governments at an unmitigated CCL (fsf31#f3); per-model FSF reports published for only two models (gdm-fs#g2). 'Less external accountability surface than Anthropic's RSP' and 'released selectively' are comparative.
entry:fsf:cov:acct.missing: comparative/analytic claim; not verifiable from sources

entry:meta-faif:cov:sec.note: Checked against v2.1 (Oct 2026), which supersedes v2: security mitigations are still set by threshold (heightened weight access controls and anti-tampering/exfiltration protections at high and critical; deployment-dependent below), with a baseline of weight-security controls for released models, and no specific controls or standards named (meta-msf#ms6, #ms7, #ms11). 'Thinner … than Anthropic or Google DeepMind' is comparative. Version/name update proposed separately (meta-v21).

entry:xai-rmf:cov:sec.note: The current edition's §2.4 states concrete commitments the note omits (xai-fw#w3–w6); the comparative clause is unverifiable. Proposal xai-sec replaces it with the documented facts.

faq:what-is-sandbagging-in-ai-safety.note: Definition and IASR Feb 2026 flag supported (iasr2026#i1–i3). FSF v2.0 never mentions Apollo, scheming or sandbagging (fsf20#v2), so 'adopted across … FSF v2' is unsupported; proposal faq-sandbag restates what sources show.

text:layer-6:tooltip.note: Lab frameworks are voluntary documents, but SB 53 bars large frontier developers from materially false statements about implementing or complying with their frontier AI framework (S-0150#20). Neither Meta's v2.1 nor xAI's Jun 2026 edition says it is the developer's SB 53 framework (meta-msf#ms11, xai-fw#w11); Anthropic and OpenAI publish separate compliance frameworks (P-0043, deferred to Jan 2027). Whether SB 53 reaches the Layer 6 documents remains undecided.
text:layer-6:tooltip.missing: Maintainer decision on P-0043 (deferred to 2027-01-15) and a source showing whether any Layer 6 framework is the developer's SB 53 / RAISE frontier AI framework; until then 'enforceable only … by its board or by reputational pressure' cannot be confirmed.
